hook.text: The Saffir-Simpson scale rates hurricanes from Category 1 (minimal) to Category 5 (catastrophic) by wind speed.

buildup.text: Category 1 starts at 119 km/h; Category 5 begins at 252 km/h—each step carries significantly more damage potential.

discovery.text: Major hurricanes (Category 3–5) account for only about 20% of landfalls but cause over 80% of total damage.

twist.text: The scale only measures wind—not storm surge, rainfall, or flooding, which often cause more deaths than wind does.

climax.text: Hurricane Harvey in 2017 was only Category 4 at landfall, but its record rainfall caused catastrophic flooding.

punchline.text: Category number tells wind speed—not the whole danger story.

quiz.question: What does the Saffir-Simpson scale measure?
